messages:
maria (support): FYI customer CanvasAI reports streaming responses cutting off mid-token. Browser reconnects and receives a duplicate partial continuation. Billing shows a spike. Trace id: rwd-ct-2026-03-17-4213
noah (eng-sre): Can you paste raw request/response headers + the gateway trace id? Which SDK or curl did they use?
maria (support): They used our JS browser SDK v0.9.1. Repro steps they gave: open SSE to /v1/stream, keep-alive: false, then simulate slow rendering by blocking main thread for ~3s, then resume. Edge logs show "writev: EAGAIN" and connection logged as HTTP/1.1 200 then immediate FIN.
li (eng-runtime): writev EAGAIN on the worker socket suggests the kernel send buffer filled. Any 502s from upstream proxy or 499s?
maria (support): No 502s. Access logs only show 200 for each attempt, but stream truncated and client retried, producing another 200. Billing shows two partial responses charged.
noah (eng-sre): Do we have connection-level metrics? sendq/rcvbuf sizes, socket queues, kernel version on pool hosts? Could be small sndbuf + Nagle interaction.
li (eng-runtime): If app sees EAGAIN we should confirm whether it's EAGAIN vs EWOULDBLOCK vs SIGPIPE in logs. A pcap/tcpdump would help. Also which libc and netstack optimizations are enabled on the pool?
maria (support): App logs: "ERROR: writev failed: EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)" then "stream aborted: client closed connection". Customer on a tight window; asked for immediate mitigations before we collect pcap.
sam (support-ops): Short-term mitigation: reduce per-chunk write sizes (smaller writev batches) so individual syscalls are less likely to overflow send buffer. Also enable periodic lightweight SSE pings (SSE-style comment pings) every 10s to keep browser internals draining.
li (eng-runtime): Agreed. We can also enable non-blocking write backoff: on EAGAIN, schedule a retry in ~50ms instead of aborting. There's an env flag STREAM_SOFT_FLOW=true which toggles soft-flow behavior.
noah (eng-sre): For billing, add an idempotency token on reconnects and a server-side debounce window (~2s) so quick reconnects don't produce duplicate charges. Also mark partial streams in telemetry and exclude from billing until a final chunk is confirmed.
maria (support): Can we provide a minimal curl repro? Customer said browser-only but they want something they can run locally.
li (eng-runtime): Try this (note the --no-buffer):

```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=small
# then in another terminal, pause reading from the socket for 3s (e.g., run a blocking script that prevents draining)
```

Stopping the client-side drain will cause the server to hit the kernel send buffer and produce EAGAIN in runtime logs.
noah (eng-sre): If the customer can run Node, this reproducer stalls the event loop and reliably simulates slow consumer in browsers:

```
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (m) => {
  // block main thread for 3s
  const t = Date.now();
  while (Date.now() - t < 3000) {}
  console.log(m.data);
};
```

That should spike sendq and hit the same path.
maria (support): I'm sharing both snippets now. Any configuration we can flip on hosted to reduce customer impact before code changes ship?
li (eng-runtime): I can flip STREAM_SOFT_FLOW=true on the affected worker pool (canary first). Also enable ephemeral SSE pings (send ":\n\n" every 10s) so browser buffers remain active.
noah (eng-sre): I'll open an ops ticket to grant CanvasAI a billing credit for duplicate partial charges while we investigate. OPS-4521.
michelle (support): Customer is OK with a canary change as long as we monitor latency and errors. Please post rollout + rollback steps.
li (eng-runtime): Rollout plan: 1) enable STREAM_SOFT_FLOW on 10% of pool (5 workers) 2) add 10s SSE ping 3) monitor EAGAIN rate + truncated-streams metric for 30m 4) if metrics improve, ramp to 100% over 20 minutes. Rollback: unset STREAM_SOFT_FLOW and remove pings.
noah (eng-sre): I'll add an alert for >3 truncated-streams/min per customer and a billing-guard alert for duplicate-charge spikes. Also recommend we add a short server-side debounce and idempotency check to reject immediate replays.
maria (support): Scheduling canary with customer at 10:30 UTC. Will collect follow-up logs and paste results here after 30m.
noah (eng-sre): If the customer can collect tcpdump on next repro that will confirm whether kernel send buffer exhaustion or an intermediary proxy is at fault. Steps: tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap host <client_ip> and attach.
maria (support): Customer acknowledged and will try to capture pcap next run. Thanks everyone.
michelle (support): :thumbsup: closing the initial escalation until canary results come in.
